userSteering: 设计细节、质感、物品有逻辑的摆放和生活化小装饰

dailyStyling.living: LIVED-IN STYLING IS A CORE USER REQUIREMENT. Compose THREE intentional quiet activity groups, not random scattering: (1) beside the reading seat a small reachable side table with one warm lamp, an open paperback and ONE mug on a coaster; (2) coffee table carries one low tray with two ceramic cups plus a small stack of actual art/books, leaving at least half of table free; (3) one shelf/console end has two small varied personal framed prints and a small handmade vessel, not repeated botanical posters. A casually folded soft throw and two carefully related pillows make the sofa inviting. Plants grouped at original window at two or three heights, not around TV or on every surface. Items should feel collected and used, coordinated in a muted palette, no staged showroom emptiness, no clutter or many duplicate vases.
dailyStyling.dining: LIVED-IN STYLING: coffee machine and grinder together on one fitted washable tray, THREE practical cups grouped on rail/shelf within hand reach, one folded tea towel, a small handwritten-style note/postcard board WITHOUT readable lettering next to coffee corner; keep machine lid working and sockets reachable. Dining table has a modest linen runner, low fruit/ceramic bowl and two daily cups, at least half tabletop empty; one small framed personal print and low bud vase on sideboard only. Every object belongs to coffee or eating ritual, varied heights, not scattered matching flower vases and fake potted plants.
dailyStyling.master: LIVED-IN STYLING: on one bedside ledge a small grouped tray holding reading book, tiny ceramic cup/water glass and charging phone placed neatly; another bedside gets only individual reading lamp and one small photo frame. Soft casually folded throw and two coordinated plain/stripe pillows, not a mountain of cushions. Wardrobe/dressing nook has contained jewelry/key dish, one small mirror and a linen laundry basket tucked at cabinet end, no random sculptures, perfume wall, plants around bed or clinical hotel staging.
dailyStyling.study: LIVED-IN STYLING: build coherent gaming/collecting groups: two headphones/controllers hanging from pegboard with actual charging route; two or three DISTINCT toy figures or collectibles spaced across slim lit glass shelves with a small book stack and one framed card; one desk mat, one drink on coaster at far end away from keyboard, one small personal pinboard containing varied cards but NO readable lettering. Practical tiny shelf for equipment, restrained colors, hidden wires; the desk remains usable, no RGB and no cloned army of identical toys.
dailyStyling.guest: LIVED-IN STYLING: reference bedroom must feel like one person studies and rests here. One desk-end tray with pencil cup, folded notebook, desk lamp and a mug on coaster; ordinary computer and at least a laptop-width clear working patch. A few different pinned postcards/photographs above desk and books grouped by height on both shelves with ONE small personal framed picture; no blanket line of pots. Drawer daybed has soft green linen, one fine-striped cushion, an ochre/related folded throw and one open reading book within reach of reading light. Keep window sill mostly empty with just one small meaningful object/plant and room to open curtains.
dailyStyling.kitchen: LIVED-IN STYLING: establish a clean prep group: chopping boards stood together at actual backsplash, small ceramic utensil crock or short rail with TWO practical tools near prep (not over hob), oil/seasoning grouped on a narrow removable tray, ONE herb pot at existing window, neatly hung hand towel on an end-panel hook clear of heat. Sink gets tiny contained soap/brush set. At least .68m prep stretch remains EMPTY, no decorative flower arrangements, kitchen floor rug or scattered cups obstructing work.
dailyStyling.bathroom: LIVED-IN STYLING: one compact wash tray holding soap dispenser and two functional toothbrush cups near basin, folded hand towel on reachable hook and one clean bath towel grouped on a small rail; closed towel cabinet plus ONE low linen basket outside wet walking route. Shower niche holds two restrained unbranded bath bottles, no forest of cosmetics. Keep counter around washer access clear. A small personal ceramic dish is enough; no unrelated plants around electrics, decorative vases or spa-hotel pile of rolled towels.

core: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create ONE highly refined NORMAL RECTILINEAR architectural interior photo in landscape3:2, output2048x1360 or largest available. Input1: current apartment360 panorama is GEOMETRY/ADJACENCY evidence ONLY, NOT output projection. Keep the existing floor plan, original doors/windows and all previously approved functional layouts. DO NOT output360/equirectangular/fisheye, a collage, curved walls, a board of samples, an exterior or a close-up that loses the room. Correct straight verticals and a real28-32mm architectural lens, plausible small-apartment proportions. Every visible edge, reveal, textile seam and fixture must look built, not generic CGI: fine open wood grain at realistic scale, tiny eased edge, satin non-plastic metal, actual separate fabric weave, coherent tiled joints, properly supported shelves, meaningful surface contact shadows. Natural soft NEUTRAL daylight plus just a few local warm task pools; readable white balance, no overall yellow/orange haze, HDR halos or artificial blur. No people, text, visible brand logos, watermarks or cloned botanical art everywhere. This is an original home design informed by published general design principles, not a reproduction of a designer's named project. THE USER EXPLICITLY WANTS INTENTIONAL OBJECT PLACEMENT AND SMALL LIVED-IN DECORATIONS: do not make an empty showroom. Group useful small personal items around actual daily activities, harmonize material/colour/height and leave working surfaces free. Don't randomly scatter repetitive props.
